Sureswar Roy vs Mr. Tapan Dutta Gupta on 2 April, 2026
 34-36.

In Re: Application under Section 389(1) of the Code of
 Criminal Procedure, 1973 / Section 430(1) of the Bharatiya
 Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023.

In the matter of : Sureswar Roy. ...applicant/appellant.
 And
 Mr. Tapan Dutta Gupta,
 Mr. Parvej Anam,
 Ms. Rituparna Ghosh,
 Mr. Sourav Sardar, ...for the Applicant/Appellant.
 (in Cra (Db) 487 of 2025 &
 Cra (Db) 43 of 2026)
 Mr. Angshuman Chakraborty
 Mr. S.S. Saha, ...for the applicant/appellant.
 (in Cra (Db) 18 of 2026)
 Ms. Faria Hossain,
 Ms. Rituparna Saha, ...for the State.
 (in Cra (Db) 18 of 2026)
 Mr. Amajit De, ...for the de facto complainant.

(in CRA (DB) 18 of 2026 &
 CRA (DB) 43 of 2026)
 Dictated by Arijit Banerjee, J.
In re : I.A. No. CRAN 1 of 2026 (in CRA (DB) 18 of 2026, Fatema Khatoon @ Fatema Bibi.)
1.
The victim is the first wife of the husband of the petitioner who is the second wife.
The petitioner was convicted along with other accused persons under Sections 498A/302/120B/34 of the Indian Penal Code and sentenced to suffer imprisonment for life.
She now prays for suspension of sentence.
2. The petitioner says that she has no role to play in the murder of the victim.
She was not a party to the alleged conspiracy to murder the victim.

She produces copy of an order dated March 24, 2026,
passed by us in CRAN 1 of 2026 filed in connection with CRA (DB) 487 of 2025, whereby a co-convict who is alleged to be one of the shooters, was granted bail.
She says that she stands on a far better footing than the said person namely, Sureswar Roy.
3. Learned State counsel and learned advocate for the de facto complainant oppose the bail prayer.
They say that the petitioner was very much a party to the conspiracy to eliminate the first wife of the petitioner's husband.
No leniency should be shown to her.

sentences.text: 4. We have considered the rival contentions of the parties and the material-on-record.

On a prima facie assimilation of the evidence-on-record and the facts and circumstances of the case, we are of the view that it cannot be said that the petitioner does not have an arguable case at all, in support of her defence.
We also see that she stands on a far better footing than Sureswar Roy who has been granted bail.
Further, the petitioner was all along on bail during the trial and it is nobody's case that she ever misused the privilege of bail.
5. Hence, we allow the prayer for suspension of sentence of the petitioner.

6. It is thus ORDERED that the applicant/appellant namely, Fatema Khatoon @ Fatema Bibi shall be released on bail upon furnishing a bond of Rs. 10,000/- (Rupees Ten Thousand) with two sureties of like amount each, one of whom must be local, to the satisfaction of the Learned Chief Judicial Magistrate, North 24-Parganas at Barasat subject to the condition that the applicant shall remain within the jurisdiction of North 24-Parganas, except for the purpose of attending court proceedings and she shall co-operate with the Investigating Officer until further orders.

She shall be personally present or shall be represented by her counsel during hearing of the appeal and she shall surrender before the Trial Court as and when called for in connection with the present appeal.

7. The department is directed to forward a copy of this order to the Superintendent of the concerned Correctional Home for immediate release of the applicant/appellant unless she is wanted in connection with any other case.

8. We clarify that the observations made by us in this order are only for the purpose of disposing of the application for suspension of sentence and the same shall have no relevance at the final hearing of the appeal.
9. The application being I.A. No. CRAN 1 of 2026 is, accordingly, disposed of.
10. All parties shall act in terms of server copy of the order downloaded from the official website of this Court.
(Apurba Sinha Ray, J.) (Arijit Banerjee, J.)
